title: Writing your report | Nature Portfolio (Nature Communications reviewer guidelines)

extracted.subtask_description: Sets out the criteria editors use reviewer reports to assess, structured around whether data quality, level of support for conclusions, and significance survive comparison to the existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of support for the conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether sufficiently strong evidence is provided for the authors' claims and all appropriate controls have been included, as one of three factors editors ask reviewers to keep in mind (alongside quality of data and potential significance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity - soundness of the data-to-conclusion interpretive leap
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Your evaluation of the validity and robustness of the data interpretation and conclusions. If you feel there are flaws that prohibit the manuscript's publication, please describe them in detail.' The core claim-vs-evidence judgment: reviewers are asked directly whether the interpretive leap from data to conclusion is sound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance claims checked against existing literature
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Your view on the potential significance of the conclusions for the field and related fields. If you think that other findings in the published literature compromise the manuscript's significance, please provide relevant references.' Ties novelty/significance claims to an explicit check against the existing literature - a reviewer who believes a claimed contribution is undercut by prior work is expected to cite it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim cannot be evaluated if underlying data is inaccessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers have 'the right to view the data and code that underlie the work if it would help in the evaluation, even if these have not been provided with the submission,' and should contact the editor if essential data are not available before submitting the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim cannot be evaluated, let alone accepted, if its underlying evidence is inaccessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength and comprehensiveness of statistical tests (analytical approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the strength of the analytical approach, 'including the validity and comprehensiveness of any statistical tests.'

rubrics_metrics.name: References evaluated as a distinct dimension from clarity/context
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Your view on whether the manuscript references previous literature appropriately.' Treated as a distinct evaluative dimension from 'clarity and context,' signaling that citation appropriateness (are prior claims cited, and cited accurately/fairly) is its own checkable criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scope-of-assessment disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to flag any part of the manuscript, data, or analyses that falls outside their expertise or that they were unable to assess fully - an explicit scope-of-review disclosure so editors know which claims went unchecked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments must not contradict comments to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential comments to the editor are reserved for sensitive information and must never contradict the comments given to the authors - i.e., a reviewer cannot privately flag an unsupported claim to the editor while telling the authors the claim is fine.
